picks.what_it_is: Tribal Persian Hashtrood Azari village rug, 285 x 112 cm, hand-knotted wool pile, natural dyes (per listing). Three hooked medallions on a charcoal spine, madder field with blue and cream sub-medallions, cream floral border.
picks.condition: Pile looks full and even, colours bright, ends and sides look tidy, back shows a sound weave. No wear seen, but no close-up of the fringes.
picks.key_photo_findings: 5 photos looked at. Design and colours match the listing. No label or tag to read (normal for a rug); the ID rests on the listing text. Back (photo 5) shows even knotting, and no repairs seen.
picks.comps_dropped: All 3 checked with WebFetch and curl. Prices and dates match what the valuer said, but none is the same item, so none can set a KEEP max. Dropped: lot 1040 29 Jul 2026 Hossainabad runner 286 x 76 cm $310 hammer (different region, 36 cm narrower); lot 972 19 Aug 2026 Mir Seraband runner 285 x 83 cm $170 hammer (city design, narrower); lot 1055 29 Jul 2026 Joshagan runner 333 x 108 cm $540 hammer (city weave, longer). As a rough guide, Armitage hand-knotted runners around 285 cm long have sold for $170 to $540 hammer lately.
picks.working: No same-item sold comp survives, so KEEP max = 0 and FLIP max = 0, and there is no maximum bid. Background only, not a comp: the closest local result is $310 hammer x 1.22 = $378.20 all-in for a narrower tribal runner. If a Hashtrood comp turns up at around $300 or more, this becomes a sensible keeper at up to about $300 hammer. WebSearch budget used up (200 of 200), so no outside comps could be checked.
picks.asking_note: Estimate 650-850. Armitage estimates on similar rugs have run well above the result (the $310 runner had a 500-750 estimate).
picks.confidence_reason: Clear ID from the listing plus photos, but no same-item sold comp.
picks.question_for_armitage: Any moth damage, stains, repairs or worn patches, and are both ends and fringes intact? Can it be posted, or is it pickup only from Invermay?
